plan: My private value is $34. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth. With only one round and no prior history, bidding $34 minimizes my risk of overpaying while maximizing my chance of winning at a fair price.

My private value is $28. To maximize profit, I want to win only if my bid allows positive expected value. Since the third-highest bid determines payment, I'll bid slightly above my true value to increase winning probability. A bid around $30-$32 balances potential profit and risk. This strategy ensures I only win when the payment is less than my value, protecting my potential earnings.

My private value is $14. To maximize profit, I want to bid strategically. Since the winner pays the third-highest bid, I'll aim to bid slightly above my value but not excessively. The goal is to win only if the price is below my value. I'll bid $15.50 - this gives me a small buffer above my value and increases my chances of winning while minimizing potential losses. The bid is close to my true value but allows some strategic flexibility.
